_README: Additions to the Waypoint Ledger price table, assembled 2026-09-08. Same law as prices.json: every figure was read out of the cited CMS file or is the product of two figures read in it, with the inputs printed on the face of the coverage statement. Nothing is estimated, inflated, interpolated or recalled. SOURCE FILES, downloaded and hashed at assembly time: (1) https://www.cms.gov/files/zip/rvu26c-updated-06-30-2026.zip  SHA256 d45a158e02694c1539e7f88192c611883e377181eda86dc213359707bcacbacb  containing PPRRVU2026_Jul_nonQPP.csv SHA256 b7d197e73211ef6854c213c267d5fa9dec8df995db8e1ee7d44c0556ad7cee21 — physician fee schedule RVUs and the conversion factor; (2) https://www.cms.gov/files/zip/26clabq3.zip  SHA256 3abf41e0c97068c8551055591db21d806fe20aa409eec9278e8e24891d463f1f  containing PUF_CLFS_CY2026_Q3V1.csv SHA256 f5a090789c40fe791b478a735c7cf5399e86726adc788f11829435cb0ca4d7d5 — clinical laboratory fee schedule payment amounts. The conversion factor $33.4009 was READ from the CONV FACTOR column of the RVU file, where it is identical on every line, and it matches the factor already used by the 24 derived rows in prices.json. PFS rows are DERIVED (total non-facility RVU x conversion factor, GPCIs 1.000) and only codes carrying status indicator A were included. Lab rows are VERIFIED (the payment amount read directly). data/verify_additions.py re-reads both CMS files and recomputes every value_usd here.

items.label: First visit with a new doctor, straightforward problem
items.geography: United States, national (geographic practice cost indices set to 1.000)
items.population: Medicare Part B fee-for-service beneficiaries
items.coverage_statement: A first appointment with a doctor who has never seen you before, for a straightforward problem. HOW THIS NUMBER WAS MADE: CMS does not publish a dollar column in the physician fee schedule. It publishes Relative Value Units and a conversion factor and defines the payment as their product. This figure is 2.25 Total non-facility RVUs x $33.4009 (the CY2026 conversion factor for a non-qualifying APM), at national geographic practice cost indices of 1.000. The RVU total is itself the sum of 0.93 work + 1.25 non-facility practice expense + 0.07 malpractice RVUs, all four figures read in the CMS file on the line for CPT 99202 (status indicator A, active and separately payable). The multiplication is ours, so this is marked DERIVED rather than VERIFIED. You can redo it yourself. This is the clinician's fee in a freestanding office. If the visit happened in a hospital-owned clinic, the hospital bills a separate facility fee on top of it. Who this describes: people on Medicare fee-for-service — that is, people 65 and older, plus people under 65 who qualified through 24 or more months of disability benefits or who have end-stage kidney disease. Who it does NOT describe: almost everyone this tool is built for. A diagnostic odyssey falls hardest on working-age adults, who are overwhelmingly on employer coverage, a Marketplace plan, Medicaid, or uninsured — and none of those prices are in this figure. Read it as a PRICE FLOOR, not as your bill: commercial insurance normally pays more than Medicare, and an uninsured person is billed the provider's charge instead, which is routinely several times this amount.
